summary.headline: How GPUs Work: Parallel Computing from Pixels to Neural Networks
summary.executive_summary: While CPUs are optimized for sequential execution using a few complex, low-latency cores, GPUs execute thousands of simple arithmetic threads simultaneously. This massively parallel SIMD architecture, originally built for 3D polygon rasterization, now forms the computational backbone of modern Artificial Intelligence and scientific simulation.
key_takeaways: CPUs optimize for single-threaded latency, while GPUs maximize aggregate parallel throughput.
Modern GPUs contain tens of thousands of ALU cores operating under SIMD/SIMT models.
Tensor cores and specialized matrix units accelerate deep learning operations by orders of magnitude.

talking_points.title: The Chef vs. The Assembly Line
talking_points.narrative_hook: If a CPU is a master chef preparing one complex dish at lighting speed, a GPU is a factory of ten thousand cooks chopping vegetables at once.

talking_points.title: The Power of SIMD Parallelism
talking_points.narrative_hook: Originally designed to render 3D video game polygons, GPUs process massive arrays of pixels with a single broadcast instruction.

talking_points.title: Fueling the AI Revolution
talking_points.narrative_hook: Because artificial intelligence calculations are essentially giant matrix multiplications, GPUs became the turbo-engine of modern deep learning.
